title: EdgeRush config file
description:
A data plane's config file, as the development harness (`edgerush proxy --config`) reads
it: the config's sections, and the files of the certificates they name. The file and
those certificate files are read again every second; a change takes over without
dropping a request, and a file that is not valid leaves the config before it running.
Listeners are bound at the start: one that is new or has moved, or HTTP/3 turned on or
off, takes a restart.

certificates.description:
The files of each certificate that listeners and upstreams name, by its name. A key
is never written into the config file itself.

data_plane.description: The data plane's own settings; left out, each has its value.

listeners.description: Where requests come in, by name.

routes.description:
The routes of `http` and `https` listeners, in order of precedence among otherwise
equal matches; empty for none.

tcp_routes.description: The routes of `tcp` listeners: one for each.

tls_routes.description:
The routes of `tls` listeners, in order of precedence among equally specific
hostnames.

upstreams.description: The upstreams that backends and mirrors name, by name.

AccessLog.description:
Where a listener's access log goes: one JSON
line a record.

oneOf.description:
The process's standard output, which a container runtime collects; the process's own
messages go to standard error.

A file, appended to; listeners that name the same path share it. A relative path is
taken from the process's working directory. SIGUSR1 has it opened again, for
rotation.

upstream.description: The name of an upstream in the same config.

weight.description:
This backend's share of the rule's requests, relative to the other weights. Zero
is no share; if all are zero the rule has nowhere to send a request.

CertificateFiles.description:
The two files a certificate is read from, each relative to the config file's directory
unless it is absolute.

chain_file.description: The certificate, then the intermediates that lead from it towards a root, in PEM.

ClientValidation.description:
Whom a listener trusts to vouch for its clients (Gateway API's frontend validation, in
its default mode: a client without a valid certificate is refused in the handshake).

authorities.description: The certificates, in PEM, of the authorities trusted.

DataPlane.description:
The whole data plane's own settings:
bounds rather than behaviour, each with its value when left out. The control plane fills
them from the `DataPlane` resource; they reload with the rest of the config.

set_aside_ms.description:
Milliseconds an endpoint that could not be connected to is set aside before a
connect probe may bring it back; 5,000
when left out.

Filter.description: Something done to a request or its response.

oneOf.description:
Changes the headers of the request before it goes to the upstream. `Host`,
`Connection`, `Keep-Alive`, `Proxy-Connection`, `TE`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Upgrade`,
`Content-Length` and `X-Request-ID` may not be named.

add.description: Values to append to whatever the headers had.

set.description:
Headers to give one value, whatever they had. A header is named once in the three
lists.

oneOf.description:
Changes the headers of the response before it goes to the client, as the request's
are changed, and beside a `redirect` too, where `Location` may not be named.

add.description: Values to append to whatever the headers had.

set.description:
Headers to give one value, whatever they had. A header is named once in the three
lists.

oneOf.description: Sends a copy of the request to another upstream too, and throws its answer away.

fraction.description:
The share of requests copied: every one is `{ numerator: 1, denominator: 1 }`, none
a numerator of 0. The numerator is no more than the denominator.

oneOf.description: Sends the upstream another host, another path or both.

host.description: The `Host` the upstream is sent: a DNS name in lower case, with no port.

path.description: The path the upstream is sent, made from the request's.

Forward.description: A rule's requests sent on to its backends.

backends.description: Where requests go, in proportion to the weights.

retry.description: Sending a request again when its answer says to; none is never.

timeouts.description: How long its requests may take; none leaves them to the data plane's fixed clocks.

Forwarding.description:
What an HTTP listener tells its upstreams of a request's client:
who it trusts to say who their clients are, and which headers only they may send. Both
are always written out, an empty list included, since both decide who a request is
taken to come from.

trusted_only_headers.description:
Headers taken off a request that did not come from a trusted proxy: names, or the
front of one followed by `*` (`X-Forwarded-*`), matched whatever their case. The
control plane's default is `Forwarded`, `X-Real-IP` and `X-Forwarded-*`. One that
takes in a header the gateway reads itself (`Host`, `Con*`) is refused.

trusted_proxies.description:
The proxies whose `X-Forwarded-For` is believed, as ranges of their addresses:
`10.0.0.0/8`, `192.0.2.1/32` for one. Empty, no one's is. Each is written one
way: no bits set past its prefix, and an IPv4 range not as IPv6.

GrpcMethod.description:
A gRPC method, matched exactly — Gateway API's Core matching for GRPCRoute: its
service, its method, or both; at least one. A gRPC call's path is `/service/method`,
and this is matched as that path would be: both as the exact path, a service alone as
the prefix `/service`, a method alone in any service.

method.description: The method: one identifier, as a service's are.

service.description:
The fully qualified service, as `package.Service`: identifiers joined by dots, each
of ASCII letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit.

name.description: The header name; case does not matter.

value.description: The value, with no white space at either end and no control characters.

HealthCheck.description:
An active check of an upstream's endpoints. Everything is stated: how often, how long a
probe may take, and how many results in a row change an endpoint's state (HAProxy's
`rise` and `fall`; Envoy's thresholds).

healthy_threshold.description: Passes in a row that make an unhealthy endpoint healthy.

interval_seconds.description: Seconds between probes of an endpoint.

timeout_seconds.description:
Seconds a probe may take, connection and handshake included; no more than the
interval.

unhealthy_threshold.description: Failures in a row that make a healthy endpoint unhealthy.

falls_through.description:
Whether this claim stays a candidate on hosts that a more specific claim also
covers: Gateway API requires it, nginx-style Ingress does not want it.

name.description: An exact name, a wildcard (`*.example.com`), or `*` for every host.

wildcard.description:
What the `*` of a wildcard name stands for. Required for a wildcard name; without
meaning, and ignored, for any other.

Http3.description: An `https` listener's HTTP/3: the same routes and TLS, over QUIC.

alt_svc_max_age.description:
How long, in seconds, a client told over TCP that the listener serves HTTP/3 may
remember it (the `ma` of `Alt-Svc`, RFC 7838 §3.1). A day unless said otherwise, as
Envoy advertises it.

force_retry.description:
Whether every client is to prove its address with a Retry before its handshake
(RFC 9000 §8.1.2), as NGINX's `quic_retry` and HAProxy's `quic-force-retry` ask.
Otherwise only past a threshold of handshakes under way, since a Retry costs a round
trip. Off unless said.

Keepalive.description:
PINGs on an HTTP/2 upstream's idle-looking connections, as gRPC's keepalive has them.
A gRPC server takes a PING more often than every five minutes as abuse, and says so
with GOAWAY(ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM), so nothing shorter is allowed unless the backend is
said to take it.

backend_allows_short_intervals.description: That the backend takes PINGs more often than every five minutes.

interval_seconds.description: Seconds between PINGs: at least 300 unless `backend_allows_short_intervals` is said.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds a PING's answer is waited for before the connection is taken for dead.

without_calls.description:
Whether to PING a connection with no call on it too; gRPC asks this be chosen on
purpose.

Listener.description:
A place where requests come in. Hostnames are to come; until a listener can be told
from another by hostname, each needs an address of its own.

access_log.description:
Where a record of each of its requests, or each of its connections for a `tcp` or
`tls` listener, is written. Left out, nothing is logged.

address.description:
The address to listen on; `[::]:8080` is every address, IPv4 included. No two
listeners have the same one.

forwarding.description:
What an `http` or `https` listener, which must have it, tells its upstreams of a
request's client; no other may.

http3.description: HTTP/3 as well, on the same port over UDP: for an `https` listener only.

proxy_protocol.description:
Whether every connection starts with a PROXY protocol header, and whose to believe. Every listener states it, `off` included: it decides who a
connection is taken to come from.

request_id.description:
Whether an `http` or `https` listener, which must say, gives each request an ID of
its own; no other may.

tls.description: What an `https` listener presents, which it must have; no other may.

tunnel_idle_seconds.description:
How long, in seconds, a `tcp` or `tls` listener's tunnel may carry nothing either
way before both its ends are closed. An hour unless said otherwise,
as HAProxy's `timeout tunnel` is set in practice: what a tunnel carries (a database's
connection, a long poll) can be quiet for long. For those listeners only.

oneOf.description: No header is read: a connection's first bytes are its protocol's.

Every connection must start with a header, v1 or v2. Its addresses are believed
when the connection comes from these ranges (`10.0.0.0/16`, `192.0.2.1/32` for one;
written as `trusted_proxies` are), the load balancer's; from anywhere else, the
header is read and dropped, and whoever connected is the client.

LoadBalancer.description: How an upstream's endpoint is chosen for an exchange.

oneOf.description:
Two different endpoints drawn at random, and the one with fewer exchanges in flight:
the power of two choices. Steers away from an endpoint that stalls.
Each endpoint in turn.

Match.description: One way for a request to belong to a rule: all of what is stated here must hold.

grpc.description: A gRPC method, as a GRPCRoute matches one: said in place of `path`.

headers.description:
Conditions on headers; names are case-insensitive. A repeated header is judged by its
fields joined.

method.description: The method, in upper case, if it matters.

path.description:
The path; `{ prefix: / }` is how to say any path. A match says this or `grpc`:
one of the two, never both.

query.description:
Conditions on decoded query parameters; names are case-sensitive. A repeated
parameter is judged by its first occurrence.

PathChange.description:
A change to a request's path. Either replacement is a path in normal form, without `?` or
`#`.

oneOf.description: The whole path becomes this.

The rule's one match, a prefix, is replaced by this, by whole segments; it may be
empty.
This path and no other.

This path and everything below it, by whole segments: `/api` takes in `/api` and
`/api/x`, not `/apix`; `/` takes in every path.

Probe.description: What a health check asks an endpoint.

oneOf.description:
`GET` this path, in the upstream's protocol: a 2xx answer passes. Not for an upstream
of TLS routes, whose endpoints speak TLS to the client, not to the data plane.

gRPC's `grpc.health.v1.Health/Check` for this service (empty for the server as a
whole): `SERVING` passes, anything else fails. For an upstream spoken to in HTTP/2.

A connection made, and its handshake finished where the upstream has `tls`: nothing
is asked. A plain one is closed so that, as a rule, the backend
never sees it.
HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 without TLS.
HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 over TLS, told apart by ALPN.
Bytes, as they come, to the listener's one TCP route.

TLS read as far as its ClientHello and no further, to the TLS route whose
hostnames cover the name the client asks for (SNI).

ProxyProtocolVersion.description: The PROXY protocol version an upstream is sent.

oneOf.description: The text line.
The binary header.

Query.description: What becomes of a request's query when it is redirected.

oneOf.description: It goes with it, byte for byte.
It is left out.

Redirect.description:
A redirect (Gateway API's `RequestRedirect`): the client is sent elsewhere, and nothing
goes upstream. The `Location` holds what is said here and only what it needs besides:
relative when none of scheme, host and port is said, and otherwise absolute, the scheme
unsaid taken from the listener and the host from the request.

host.description: The host to send the client to: a DNS name in lower case.

path.description: The path to send the client to, made from the request's.

port.description: The port to send the client to; written only if it is not its scheme's default.

query.description: Whether the request's query goes with it.

scheme.description: The scheme to send the client to.

RequestId.description: What an HTTP listener does with `X-Request-ID`.

oneOf.description:
Every request gets an ID the gateway makes, in place of any it came with, whoever
sent it; the answer tells the client the same ID, in place of any the upstream gave.
The header is left as it is, both ways: a proxy in front can give the ID.

Retry.description:
When a request is sent again, and how often (Gateway API's HTTPRoute retry, with
gRPC's statuses beside HTTP's). A try that could not connect is sent again whatever is
named, as Gateway API asks: nothing of it reached the endpoint. Otherwise decided on an
answer's head alone: once a head has gone to the client, the request is not sent again.
Within a budget of the upstream's, and only for a body small enough to be kept.

attempts.description: Times a request may be sent again, beyond the first.

backoff_base_ms.description:
Milliseconds before the first retry; each after it waits twice as long, and as much
again at random. No more than `backoff_max_ms`.

backoff_max_ms.description:
The most milliseconds a wait may double to, before its random part is added: a wait
can come to nearly twice this.

grpc_statuses.description:
gRPC statuses, by gRPC's names (`UNAVAILABLE`), that send a call again when the
answer's head carries them.

http_statuses.description:
HTTP statuses that send it again. `502` also stands for an upstream that connected
and answered nothing; a try that ran out of time is `on_timeout`'s, not
`502`'s.

on_timeout.description:
Whether a try that ran out of time before its answer's head is sent again: the
upstream's fixed clocks for a head, or for the request's upload or the answer to
go on, running out. Stated whichever way, so that a config says what it does. `true`
needs a try to have a clock of its own: the fixed clocks, which stay while `timeouts`
states neither `request_ms` nor `backend_request_ms`, or a `backend_request_ms` above
0. A retry names at least one status, or says `true` here.

Route.description:
A route: the hosts it serves and its rules.

Routes come as an ordered list, and the order matters: it is the last tie-breaker of
precedence. The control plane emits them oldest first, then by name.

hostnames.description: The hosts served; every host is asked for by the name `*`.

listeners.description: The names of the `http` and `https` listeners whose requests this route is for.

name.description: Unique among every kind of route; what errors, status and metrics refer to.

Rule.description:
A rule: the requests it is for, what is done to them on the way, and what becomes of
them.

filters.description: What is done to a request and its response. Each kind of filter at most once.

forward.description:
Its requests sent on to its backends. A rule says this or `redirect`: one of the
two, never both.

matches.description: The rule is for a request that satisfies any one of these.

redirect.description:
Its requests answered with a redirect, said in place of `forward`. Of the filters,
only `response_header_modifier` goes with it.

Scheme.description: A scheme a redirect sends a client to.

oneOf.description: `http`.
`https`.

SlowStart.description:
Slow start: an endpoint added to an upstream
that keeps an endpoint it had, or passing its checks again after failing them, takes a
share rising linearly from a tenth of a full one to all of it over the window.

window_ms.description: How long the ramp takes, in milliseconds.

TcpRoute.description:
A route for a `tcp` listener: every connection it takes goes to these backends, as
Gateway API's TCPRoute has it.

backends.description: Where connections go, in proportion to the weights.

listeners.description: The names of the `tcp` listeners it is for.

name.description: Unique among every kind of route.

Timeouts.description:
How long a rule's requests may take (Gateway API's HTTPRoute `timeouts`). A timeout
stated takes the place of the data plane's fixed clocks for an answer's head; the idle
clocks, which find data that stopped flowing, run whatever is stated. At least one.

backend_request_ms.description:
Milliseconds a try may take, from its start — connecting, and waiting for a place on
an HTTP/2 connection, included — to its answer's head; `0` for no limit at all. No
more than `request_ms`. A try that runs out of it is sent again under a retry's
`on_timeout`. It stops at the head, not the answer's end: the answer streams to the
client as the client takes it, and a slow client is not the backend running late.

request_ms.description:
Milliseconds from the request's head arriving to its answer's end, upload, retries
and all; `0` for no limit at all.

tunnel_idle_ms.description:
Milliseconds a WebSocket may carry nothing either way once its upgrade is made,
before it is closed; an hour when not
stated. Not Gateway API's: it has no such field.

certificates.description:
The names of the certificates it can present. A client is given the
one whose names cover the name it asked for (SNI), and the first when none does or
it asked for none. No name twice.

client_validation.description:
Clients must show a certificate these authorities vouch for (mTLS); none, and any
client is served.

TlsRoute.description:
A route for a `tls` listener: the connections whose ClientHello asks for a name its
hostnames cover, as Gateway API's TLSRoute has it in passthrough mode.

backends.description: Where connections go, in proportion to the weights.

hostnames.description:
The names served, matched against the SNI as a request's host is against an HTTP
route's.

listeners.description: The names of the `tls` listeners it is for.

name.description: Unique among every kind of route.

Upstream.description: A set of endpoints that serve the same thing.

endpoints.description:
Where to connect: addresses, not names, each once. None is allowed, and means there
is nothing to send a request to — a state a running system passes through, not a
mistake.

health_check.description:
Probes of each endpoint, which keep one that fails them out of load balancing;
none is every endpoint taken as healthy.

keepalive.description:
HTTP/2 PINGs to find a dead connection before a request does; none is no PINGs. For
an upstream spoken to in HTTP/2 only.

load_balancer.description: Which endpoint takes each exchange. Always stated: it chooses behaviour.

protocol.description:
What its endpoints are spoken to in, whatever the client spoke. An upstream of TCP
and TLS routes is sent their bytes as they come: neither `http2` nor `tls`.

proxy_protocol.description:
A PROXY protocol header ahead of each tunnel's bytes, telling the backend who the
client is; none is no header. For an upstream of TCP and TLS routes only: an HTTP
route's connections carry many clients' requests.

slow_start.description:
A new or recovered endpoint's ramp to its full share; none is every endpoint at its
full share from the start.

tls.description: TLS to its endpoints; none is plain TCP.

UpstreamProtocol.description:
What an upstream is spoken to in. Unsaid, it is HTTP/1.1, as for a Kubernetes Service
port that names no application protocol.

oneOf.description: HTTP/1.1, a request at a time on each connection.

HTTP/2, many requests at once on each connection. Without TLS, by prior knowledge
(RFC 9113 §3.3): the upstream is expected to speak it from the first byte.

UpstreamTls.description:
TLS to an upstream's endpoints: whom they are expected to be, and whom to trust to say
so (Gateway API's BackendTLSPolicy: a hostname and CA certificates).

authorities.description: The certificates, in PEM, of the authorities trusted to vouch for it.

client_certificate.description:
The name of the certificate the data plane shows an endpoint that asks who it is
(mTLS); none, and it shows nothing.

server_name.description:
The name asked for (SNI), and the one an endpoint's certificate must carry: a host
name, not an address, and with no wildcard or port.

oneOf.description: This value and no other.

The values this regular expression describes as a whole: RE2-style syntax in
ASCII, with no look-around or backreferences, at most 256 KiB compiled; case matters
unless it says `(?i)`.

ValuePredicate.description: A condition on a named value: a header or a query parameter.

Wildcard.description:
What the `*` of a wildcard hostname stands for. Neither covers the bare suffix:
`*.example.com` is not `example.com`.

oneOf.description: Exactly one label, as in Ingress.
One or more labels, as in Gateway API.
